exposure: ADHD medication use (amphetamine, dexamphetamine, methylphenidate, atomoxetine, lisdexamfetamine, guanfacine) during early pregnancy
ADHD medication use (amphetamine, dexamphetamine, methylphenidate, atomoxetine, lisdexamfetamine, guanfacine) during late pregnancy
cohort: Pregnant individuals with ADHD medication use in the year before conception, who delivered singleton births between 22 and 44 gestational weeks in Norway (2009-2020) and Sweden (2007-2019).
finding: ADHD medication may modestly increase the risk of preterm birth, especially with atomoxetine early and methylphenidate late in pregnancy, and with longer durations of use.
gest_age: Singleton births delivered between 22 and 44 gestational weeks, with preterm birth defined as a live birth before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy.
